{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# NOTE: Input is an LSF submit-wrapper that *generates* a batch script and calls `bsub`.
# Below is the Flux equivalent as a single self-submitting script.

nnds=4096

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./ytopt.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from LSF:
#   #BSUB -nnodes 4096  -> -N 4096
#   #BSUB -W 30         -> -t 30m
#
# NOTE: LSF -P MED106 (project/account) not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: accounting/charging may not be applied as intended; site may require project/account out-of-band.
#
# NOTE: LSF -J ytopt (job name) not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance unaffected.
#
# NOTE: LSF -o/-e output.log/output.err not translated.
# Performance implication: none; operational implication: stdout/stderr handling follows Flux defaults unless configured at submission.
#
# NOTE: LSF -alloc_flags gpumps not translated.
# Performance implication: without the allocation flags, placement/affinity or special allocation behavior may differ, impacting performance.

JOBID=$(flux batch -N ${nnds} -n ${nnds} -t 30m --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  export OMP_NUM_THREADS=168

  # LSF used jsrun for launch on IBM systems. Under Flux, we launch the same command.
  # NOTE: This assumes `jsrun` is available in the environment and interoperates with the allocated resources.
  flux run -N ${nnds} -n ${nnds} \
    jsrun -n ${nnds} -a 1 -g 0 -c 42 -bpacked:42 -dpacked ../amg2013 -laplace -P 16 16 16 -n 100 100 100  > out.txt

  flux run -N ${nnds} -n ${nnds} \
    jsrun -n ${nnds} -a 1 -g 0 -c 42 -bpacked:42 -dpacked ../amg2013 -laplace -P 16 16 16 -n 100 100 100  > out2.txt

  flux run -N ${nnds} -n ${nnds} \
    jsrun -n ${nnds} -a 1 -g 0 -c 42 -bpacked:42 -dpacked ../amg2013 -laplace -P 16 16 16 -n 100 100 100  > out3.txt

  flux run -N ${nnds} -n ${nnds} \
    jsrun -n ${nnds} -a 1 -g 0 -c 42 -bpacked:42 -dpacked ../amg2013 -laplace -P 16 16 16 -n 100 100 100  > out4.txt

  flux run -N ${nnds} -n ${nnds} \
    jsrun -n ${nnds} -a 1 -g 0 -c 42 -bpacked:42 -dpacked ../amg2013 -laplace -P 16 16 16 -n 100 100 100  > out5.txt
fi
"
}

You MUST not make up directives that do not exist.
You MUST preserve as many options as possible from the original.

Each `flux run -N 4096 -n 4096` repeats the full-size allocation request for the step; if the enclosing allocation differs, steps may fail. If the intent is to run within the batch allocation, `flux run` should generally omit `-N` and match/fit within allocated resources.
